title: Liguria's Fuel Prices Settle as Methane's Wild 2026 Run Keeps Outpacing the Rest of Italy
dek: Petrol and diesel in Liguria are drifting back toward the national average, even as methane's 51% climb since July continues to outrun the country as a whole.
executive_summary: As of November 26, 2026, Liguria's self-service prices stand at €1.9525/L for Benzina, €2.2247/L for Gasolio, €0.918/L for GPL, and €2.159/kg for Metano — essentially flat to slightly lower than the day before, with Benzina easing 0.23% and Gasolio 0.10%, while GPL and Metano held unchanged. Against the national self-service averages of €1.9452, €2.2218, €0.8346 and €2.1147 respectively, Liguria is trading at a premium across the board, from a negligible 0.38% on Benzina up to a full 10.0% on GPL and 2.1% on Metano.

Zoom out to the weekly data tracked since the week of July 20, and a clearer story emerges: Benzina and Gasolio in Liguria have moved in near lockstep with the national trend — petrol down roughly 1.6% and diesel up roughly 2.3% over the period, both within a couple of tenths of a point of the national move. Metano is the real outlier. Liguria's methane price has climbed 51.1% since tracking began, versus a 40.8% rise nationally, flipping the region from trading at a discount to methane buyers in midsummer to a steady premium since late September. GPL has followed a quieter version of the same pattern, rising 10.3% in Liguria against 9.8% nationally, and has kept the region among the priciest in the country for LPG throughout.

fuel_sections.heading: Liguria's Petrol Keeps Sliding — Now a Hair Above the National Floor
paragraphs: Liguria's self-service Benzina price fell to €1.9525/L on November 26, down €0.0045 (-0.23%) from €1.9570/L the day before, continuing a gentle multi-week decline. That puts the region just €0.0073/L (+0.38%) above the national self-service average of €1.9452/L — the smallest premium of the four tracked fuels.

Looking at the weekly series since the week of July 20, Liguria's Benzina price has fallen 1.56% overall (from €1.9885 to €1.9575 per the latest weekly average), slightly outpacing the national decline of 1.28% (€1.9756 to €1.9504) over the same stretch. Both series peaked in the week of September 21 — Liguria at €2.1802, the nation at €2.1669 — before easing steadily into November; Liguria's pullback from that peak (-10.2%) has been marginally sharper than the national one (-10.0%), which is why the region has drifted from trading noticeably above the national price in September to almost matching it today.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel in Liguria Cools Off After Its September Spike
paragraphs: Gasolio eased to €2.2247/L in Liguria on November 26, down €0.0022 (-0.10%) day-over-day, and now sits just €0.0029/L (+0.13%) above the national self-service average of €2.2218/L — effectively at parity with the rest of Italy.

The weekly trend tells a similar story: Liguria's diesel price has risen 2.30% since the week of July 20 (from €2.1768 to €2.2268), almost identical to the national 2.26% rise (€2.1747 to €2.2239) over the same period. Both series spiked hard in the week of September 21 — Liguria to €2.3865, the nation to €2.3736 — before pulling back into November, Liguria by 6.69% and the nation by 6.31%. Diesel is the fuel where Liguria has tracked the national average most closely all year.

fuel_sections.heading: LPG's Slow Grind Upward Leaves Liguria Paying a Premium
paragraphs: GPL held steady at €0.918/L in Liguria on November 26, unchanged from the prior day, but the region continues to pay noticeably more than the rest of the country: the national self-service average is €0.8346/L, a gap of €0.0834/L, or 10.0%, that has persisted for weeks.

Since the week of July 20, Liguria's GPL price has climbed 10.34% (from €0.832 to €0.918), modestly outpacing the national rise of 9.80% (€0.7592 to €0.8336). Unlike Benzina and Gasolio, GPL in Liguria has shown no autumn pullback — it has simply ratcheted upward through a series of step-changes, notably in mid-August and again in mid-November, and the region's premium over the national average has widened from essentially nothing in July to roughly 10 cents a litre today.

fuel_sections.heading: Methane's Breakout Year: Liguria Outpaces the Nation
paragraphs: Metano held at €2.159/kg in Liguria on November 26, flat day-over-day, and now sits €0.0443/kg (+2.1%) above the national self-service average of €2.1147/kg.

This is the standout trend of the year for Liguria: methane has risen 51.1% since the week of July 20 (from €1.429 to €2.159), well ahead of the 40.8% national increase (€1.4999 to €2.1115) over the same stretch. The region actually traded below the national price for most of the summer — by as much as 4.7% in the week of July 20 — before crossing above it by late September, spiking to a 5-7% premium in early October, and settling into a steadier 2.2% premium for the past month. No other fuel in Liguria has moved this far from where it started, or diverged this much from the national trend.

network_section.heading: Fewer Stations, Steady Coverage: Liguria's Reporting Rate Holds Above the National Average
paragraphs: Liguria had 539 registered fuel stations as of November 26, 2026, of which 492 reported prices that day — a reporting rate of 91.3%. That is comfortably above the national reporting rate of 90.5% (21,691 of 23,977 registered stations), suggesting the region's relatively small, dense network of pumps keeps data flowing more consistently than the national picture as a whole.

Over the months tracked, Liguria's registered count has stayed remarkably stable, oscillating narrowly between 537 and 540 stations, while the number actively reporting prices on any given day has ranged from about 486 to 493 — a swing of roughly 1.5%. That tight band points to a mature, well-monitored regional network rather than stations dropping in and out of the MIMIT feed, which makes Liguria's daily averages unusually reliable for day-to-day comparison.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: Zero Spreadsheets, One Daily Pipeline
paragraphs: Everything in this report — the raw price data pulled from MIMIT's daily feed, the rotation that selects a new Italian region to spotlight each day, the weekly trend analysis comparing that region against the national average, and the prose you are reading right now — is produced automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. No analyst manually downloads a CSV, builds a pivot table, or writes up a summary; the pipeline ingests the data, computes the figures, and drafts the narrative from them end to end.

That stands in sharp contrast to how this kind of regional price tracking is traditionally done: a manually maintained spreadsheet, updated by hand whenever someone remembers to check the source data, with charts that go stale between updates and no capacity to rotate through 20 regions or recompute multi-week trends on demand. This project exists to show that an AI-assisted pipeline can replace that manual spreadsheet entirely, publishing a live, interactive dashboard and a fresh written report every single day without a human reopening a spreadsheet.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Liguria
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just the starting point — use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or another Operator/Brand and dig into whichever slice of Italy's fuel market you care about.

pull_quote: Metano in Liguria has surged 51% since July — nearly ten points faster than the national rise — flipping the region from a summer discount to a lasting premium at the pump.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Liguria.

The standout number: methane (Metano) prices in Liguria have climbed 51% since tracking began in July, outpacing the 41% rise seen nationally, and flipping the region from trading below the national average in midsummer to a consistent premium since late September. Petrol and diesel, by contrast, have moved almost in lockstep with the rest of Italy all year.

Fuel Dashboard is a live, interactive site that tracks petrol, diesel, LPG and methane prices across all 20 Italian regions, every province, municipality and major brand, updated every morning. Each day it also rotates through a different region and publishes a full written report like this one, grounded in that day's real numbers.

Here's the part I think is actually interesting: none of this is run by a person updating a spreadsheet. The entire pipeline, fetching the data, picking the region, computing the weekly trends, writing the report, and publishing the site, runs unattended every morning, built with Claude Code. No analyst, no spreadsheet, no manual chart-making. It is a live demonstration of what is possible when an AI agent owns an entire daily workflow end to end, instead of just speeding up one step of a manual process.
